Clinical interpretation
Across 17 studies, summary sensitivity was 65.762% (95% confidence interval 59.020% to 71.923%) and summary specificity was 80.975% (95% confidence interval 73.885% to 86.492%).
These are average operating characteristics across the included study thresholds. The Reitsma bivariate and HSROC formulations are equivalent parameterizations of this model; that equivalence does not assume a common threshold. texts.Clinical interpretation:
This Reitsma bivariate meta-regression jointly models sensitivity and false-positive rate across 17 studies using 2 moderators.
Moderator coefficients are reported separately for sensitivity and specificity as odds ratios with confidence intervals. Reference rows equal 1; continuous-moderator estimates describe a one-unit increase.

texts.small-study.method-details:
Rücker AS+RE test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: ASD effect on native ASD standard error
  Weighting: native AS+RE additive REML weights
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 15.00
  Exact p-value: 0.60854439
  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='ASD', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); meta::metabias(x=prepared.ASD.model, method.bias='Thompson', k.min=10, level=0.95)

Peters test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: 1/(n.e+n.c), with native Peters seTE=sqrt(1/(event.e+event.c)+1/(non-events.e+non-events.c))
  Weighting: 1/Peters seTE^2
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 15.00
  Exact p-value: 0.80833677
  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='OR', incr=0.5, method.incr='only0', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); prepared.OR.model$TE <- prepared.effects; prepared.OR.model$seTE <- prepared.standard.errors; meta::metabias(x=prepared.OR.model, method.bias='Peters', k.min=10, level=0.95)
texts.small-study.methods-not-applicable: Harbord test: Unavailable: REML log-OR tau^2 is above 0.1; use Rücker AS+RE.
